paragraphs.mainIdea: The man who leads the town tells the old story of the country and why the Games exist.
paragraphs.simple: The man who leads the town and the woman from the city sit down, and they look at a chair with no one in it. At 2 he reads the same story as every year. There was a country called North America. Bad weather, fires, dry years, and war left little food. From that came this country, a rich city with 13 districts around it. Then the districts rose up. 12 lost, and number 13 was gone. A treaty made new laws, and the Games, so people would not forget. Each district must send one girl and one boy. The 24 children are shut in a huge place in the open and must fight until one is left. The city does this so the districts remember they have no power.

paragraphs.context: a special bird called a jabberjay that had
paragraphs.mainIdea: The city made animals that could remember people's words and bring them back.
paragraphs.simple: In the war, the city made animals into weapons. People call them mutts. One was a jabberjay. It could hear a whole talk and say it again. They were sent where the city's enemies could not be seen. They flew back with the words. When people understood, they told them lies. The city stopped, and the animals were left in the wild.

paragraphs.context: these killer wasps were spawned in a lab
paragraphs.mainIdea: The thing above her may be the small flying animals the city made to kill.
paragraphs.simple: She looks up and sees a shape like a small animal on a tree, and she hears a low sound. It is a home of small flying animals that can hurt you. In the Games it is probably not a normal one. Tracker jackers were made by the city and left near the districts in the war, like things that go off if you step on them. They are big and gold, and one hit makes a hard spot the size of a small round food. A few can kill. If you live, the bad stuff from them can make you see things that are not there, and even drive you mad. They also follow anyone who touches their home. That is why they are called trackers.

paragraphs.context: Deep in the meadow, under the willow
paragraphs.mainIdea: She says a soft song about a safe green place, while the girl dies.
paragraphs.simple: The song puts the girl in a green field under a tree, on a soft bed of green, and tells her to close her eyes. When she opens them, the sun will be up. The place is safe and warm. Pretty plants keep bad things away. Her dreams are sweet, and morning will take her troubles away. It is the place where she is loved. She says the same soft things again as the girl goes still.

sentences.context: you can hear a pin drop, and I'm feeling
sentences.simple: Everyone goes still at once, and she feels so afraid that she may be sick, hoping her name will not be read.
sentences.grammar: One long line joins three moments: they pull in air, the place goes still, and she hopes it is not her name.

sentences.context: if I could only hold out until May
sentences.simple: She told herself that if she could last until her birthday, she could get food for the family.
sentences.grammar: She is looking back at a hope she kept saying: last until one day, and then the food would come.

sentences.context: so a person could conceivably watch the whole thing
sentences.simple: The shows are spread through the day so someone could watch them all, but only people in the city really can.
sentences.grammar: The line says what the plan is for, and then it takes that plan back for everyone outside the city.

sentences.context: As long as you can find yourself, you'll never starve
sentences.simple: Her father joked that if she can find this plant, she will always have food.
sentences.grammar: He uses her name as a joke, because the plant and the girl share it.

sentences.context: not only dirt but at least three layers of skin
sentences.simple: They move their hands on her so hard that they take off what is on her skin and even some skin, and they also shape the ends of her hands and take off her hair.
sentences.grammar: One subject, this, has a long list of things that were done to her body.

sentences.context: while I can't pull it up, I know some bad memory
sentences.simple: Even as she says she does not know the girl, her body goes hard, and she knows a bad memory is there.
sentences.grammar: She says one thing, and at the same time her body tells her the other thing.

sentences.context: as if ready to take wing at the slightest sound
sentences.simple: The small girl stands on her toes with her arms out, like something about to fly if she hears anything.
sentences.grammar: The picture of a flying thing is how the line shows that the girl is ready to run.

sentences.context: the animals would still be afoot when the snow
sentences.simple: The only animal she had shot was one small one, but the animals would still be out when the white cold covered her other food.
sentences.grammar: The line starts with how little she shot, then turns with but to the harder time that was coming.

sentences.context: the boy who risked a beating to give me bread
sentences.simple: She lists the kind things the boy has done: the food, the ride, the girl who cannot speak, and telling the man who helps them that she can find animals.
sentences.grammar: The line is a list of who he is, with no main event yet. Each who adds one more kind act.

sentences.context: I could slip away now, without him noticing
sentences.simple: She could leave without him hearing her, but the night air is so sweet that she cannot stand going back to her room.
sentences.grammar: Could starts a chance she does not take, and but gives the reason she stays.

sentences.context: a bright orange backpack that could hold anything
sentences.simple: There is little to take, and she is so angry that she runs for a bag of a strong color because she cannot bear to leave with nothing.
sentences.grammar: So and so put two feelings in a line, and because gives the reason she runs.

sentences.context: when all along, all along he'd planned
sentences.simple: She remembers him telling her not to fight for the supplies, while the whole time he had planned to throw himself into the fight.
sentences.grammar: When sets what he said next to the truth she sees only now, and all along is said twice.

sentences.context: hoping the lack of air will quell what I haven't
sentences.simple: She does not want to leave the hot cover, so she pushes it into her bag and hopes no air will put out the last of the fire.
sentences.grammar: The line puts a fear, a risk, and a hope one after another, each one held by the one before.

sentences.context: instead of one string I see three
sentences.simple: She tries to set the shot, but the bad stuff makes her see three lines, and the bad air is so strong she cannot do it.
sentences.grammar: But instead of turns the simple act into what the bad stuff does to her eyes.

sentences.context: Gale and Peeta do not coexist well together in my thoughts
sentences.simple: She wonders what her friend thought, and then she pushes it away because the two boys do not fit in her mind at the same time.
sentences.grammar: For some reason leaves the cause unsaid, and because gives the only reason she will say.

sentences.context: I could end up losing all twelve of my arrows
sentences.simple: She thinks a shot of fire might work, and then she sees she could lose every shot and still miss the oil.
sentences.grammar: The idea comes back and then when I realize takes it back in the same line.

sentences.context: so people really do tear out their hair
sentences.simple: His feeling is so huge it would look funny, people really do pull their hair, except she knows it is for her.
sentences.grammar: So starts a picture of a wild feeling, and if turns it serious because the feeling is for her.

sentences.context: whatever they do or force us to do
sentences.simple: She wants to show the city as wrong right now, and to show that some part of each child is still not theirs.
sentences.grammar: Three to-lines say what she wants, and whatever says the city can force the acts but not the whole person.

sentences.context: all right, maybe the idea of him being naked
sentences.simple: She leaves his shorts on because the leg is too big and hurts, and also, she says, because him with no clothes makes her uneasy.
sentences.grammar: All right, maybe adds a second, less sure reason after the useful one.

sentences.context: it wouldn't have been good to go carrying
sentences.simple: Even though people knew they took animals, it would have been bad to carry a huge animal through town in the day, as if they were showing off.
sentences.grammar: Even though gives the fact, and like we were says how the officials would have read the act.

sentences.context: I will stare her down as long as I can
sentences.simple: As her last act, she will look the girl in the eyes for as long as she can see, and she will not call out.
sentences.grammar: She says I will three times. Saying it again is a promise, not a new fact.

sentences.context: To say my thoughts aloud would be tipping
sentences.simple: If she says what she thinks, the audience will learn the love story was made up, and then there will be no food.
sentences.grammar: To say starts what could go wrong, and that would result gives the cost of saying it.

sentences.context: who can spin out lies so convincingly the whole
sentences.simple: This kind boy, hard to read, can lie so well that the whole country thinks he loves her, and sometimes he makes her believe it too.
sentences.grammar: Who adds fact after fact about the same boy, and the question at the end is really her own doubt.

sentences.context: who can snap a neck with a twist of his arm
sentences.simple: She means the hard boy who can break a head from the body, who beat the strong boy, and who has wanted her dead from the start.
sentences.grammar: Three who-lines add up what makes him so bad to face. The name is already known.

sentences.context: even though the mutt has begun to slide backward
sentences.simple: Even though the animal is moving back and its feet make a hard sound on the metal, she still shoots into the front of its body.
sentences.grammar: Even though is said twice, and still she fires. The fear does not stop the shot.

sentences.context: it must be Effie, it has to be Effie
sentences.simple: She throws herself at the glass and calls out, and she thinks she sees light red hair, so it must be the woman coming to save her, and then a point hits her from behind.
sentences.grammar: It must be and it has to be say the same hope twice, and when cuts the hope off.

sentences.context: not with the announcement of our victory, but with me
sentences.simple: She is glad that the film ends not with them winning, but with her hitting the glass and calling his name.
sentences.grammar: Not with, but with sets the expected ending against the picture they actually leave her with.

hold one's tongue.meaning: To stop yourself from saying what you think.
hold one's tongue.example: So I learned to hold my tongue and to turn my features into an indifferent mask.

turn a blind eye.meaning: To act as if you do not see something.
turn a blind eye.example: Most of the Peacekeepers turn a blind eye to the few of us who hunt.

crack of dawn.meaning: The very start of the day, when the first light comes.
crack of dawn.example: He must have been at the bakery at the crack of dawn to trade for it.

black market.meaning: A place where people buy and sell against the law.
black market.example: Discuss little more than trades in the Hob, which is the black market where I make most of my money.

skin and bones.meaning: So little to eat that you can see the shape of the body under the skin.
skin and bones.example: I try to remember that when all I can see is the woman who sat by, blank and unreachable, while her children turned to skin and bones.

might as well.meaning: There is no strong reason not to. It would be just as good.
might as well.example: The reaping isn't until two. May as well sleep in.

out of one's wits.meaning: So afraid that you cannot think.
out of one's wits.example: We have to joke about it because the alternative is to be scared out of your wits.

on good terms.meaning: Friendly with someone, with no fight between you.
on good terms.example: We might do a tad better elsewhere, but we make an effort to keep on good terms with Greasy Sae.

turn up one's nose.meaning: To act as if something is not good enough for you.
turn up one's nose.example: No one in the Seam would turn up their nose at a good leg of wild dog.

keep to oneself.meaning: To stay away from other people and not share your life.

make out.meaning: To be able to see, hear, or understand.
make out.example: At first, I have no idea what she's pointing to, but then, about fifteen feet up, I make out the vague shape.

make out well.meaning: To do all right. To get what you need.

at stake.meaning: At risk. It may be lost.
at stake.example: But there are others, too, who have no one they love at stake.

keep tabs on.meaning: To watch people and keep a record of them.
keep tabs on.example: The reaping is a good opportunity for the Capitol to keep tabs on the population as well.

hear a pin drop.meaning: So still that even a very small sound would be heard.
hear a pin drop.example: The crowd draws in a collective breath and then you can hear a pin drop.

blown to bits.example: My father knew and he taught me some before he was blown to bits in a mine explosion.

fair game.meaning: Something anyone may take. No one owns it.

stick together.example: instruction that we stick together in training.

stick it out.meaning: To keep going until a hard time ends.
stick it out.example: Then you grit your teeth and stick it out until dawn!

stick with.meaning: To stay with one choice and not change.
stick with.example: Maybe you should just stick with that.

figure out.example: try to figure out how they will survive the painful weeks to come.

end up.meaning: To come to a result you did not fully plan.
end up.example: The ride lasts about twenty minutes and ends up at the City Circle.

show off.meaning: To try to make people look at how good you are.
show off.example: Career Tributes who are showing off, clearly trying to intimidate the field.

on purpose.meaning: Not by accident. You meant to do it.
on purpose.example: We don't hunt them on purpose, but if you're attacked and you take out a dog or two, well, meat is meat.

at last.example: At last, this is over, but it isn't.

in charge.example: but the appetites of those in charge protect me.

gold mine.meaning: A thing that can bring you a lot of what you need.
gold mine.example: that goat would be a little gold mine

for good.meaning: Forever. It will not come back.
for good.example: if he's out of this for good.

drop the ball.meaning: To miss what you needed to do at an important moment.
drop the ball.example: for dropping the ball during such an emotionally charged moment.

ahead of the game.meaning: Already thinking of the next step, before the hard part.
ahead of the game.example: I need to look one step ahead of the game.

keep track.meaning: To follow something and remember it.
keep track.example: I have kept track of the boy with the bread.

track down.meaning: To find someone by following them.
track down.example: We don't want to have to track her down twice.

live with.meaning: To accept something hard and go on.
live with.example: Shoot me and go home and live with it!

out of nowhere.meaning: Suddenly, from a place you did not see.
out of nowhere.example: The hovercraft appeared out of nowhere.

all of a sudden.example: All of a sudden, I'm overwhelmed by the thought that Peeta may be already lost.

never mind.meaning: It does not matter. Forget it.

come across.meaning: To find something when you were not looking for it.
come across.example: When Gale and I come across a tracker jacker nest, we immediately head in the opposite direction.

count on.meaning: To trust that someone or something will be there.
count on.example: She's the only one who can consistently be counted on to buy wild dog.

get rid of.meaning: To remove something you do not want.
get rid of.example: My mother got rid of the vermin and he's a born mouser.

in the nick of time.example: To say I make it in the nick of time is an understatement.

hold one's ground.meaning: To stay where you are and not give in.
hold one's ground.example: But Peeta holds his ground, actually waving and smiling at the gawking crowd.
